item.title: inventory-client: detect longer next_cursor cycles in listItems
item.brief: In inventory-client, the listItems pagination loop (branch archon/4ne9w5sr-make-listitems-follow-next-cursor, commit 2250eec) only detects a next_cursor equal to the previous one. A cycle such as A to B to A would loop forever. Replace that check with a seen-set of cursors: reject with a clear error when any cursor repeats. Add a test with a fake transport where the cursor cycles over two values and expect rejection. Keep npm test passing and update the README if it describes the guard. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

item.title: Make listItems follow next_cursor
item.brief: In inventory-client, change listItems(transport) so it resolves to every item in order by requesting pages until next_cursor is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged; the first request sends no cursor. Add tests with a fake transport covering multi-page, single-page, and absent next_cursor. Update the README to document that listItems now follows pagination. Keep `npm test` passing. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief:
In inventory-api, change GET /items to cursor pagination per the shared contract: optional limit (int 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous response); body {"items": [...], "next_cursor": string|null}; items ordered by id; next_cursor null on the last page; invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add unit tests covering paging, last page, default limit, and 400 cases. Update the README to document the new parameters and response shape. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

pr.body: Approach: cursor is the id of the last item on the page; each request returns ids greater than the cursor, sorted ascending (keyset paging, stable across pages). Key files: api.py (list_items, _parse_limit, _parse_cursor, _is_digits), test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 10 tests OK at 0ca8195. Review: 3 whole-change reviewers and 1 delta reviewer; the one blocking finding (non-string query values raised AttributeError) is fixed in 0ca8195 with a regression test. Advisory follow-ups: >4300-digit limit/cursor gets Python's int-limit message (still 400); cursor is the raw id, so the README's 'opaque' wording is loose; list_items re-sorts on every request. Assumptions: the amendment asked for one reviewer, but the stage contract requires three, so three whole-change reviewers were used. The API change means existing callers of GET /items now get at most 20 items plus next_cursor.
pr.summary: Made GET /items paged: limit 1..100 (default 20), opaque cursor, next_cursor null on last page. Now: at most 20 items per default request, next_cursor for paging. Before: all items in one response. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with an error body, including non-string values.
pr.title: feat(api): add cursor pagination to GET /items
